hints.title: 1 · Trace the trust boundary
hints.body: Compare authenticated agent, ticket scope, role, and body separately. A valid ID alone is not authorization.

hints.title: 2 · Make the unit of work explicit
hints.body: A state transition and its audit must commit together. Inject an audit failure and inspect persisted state.

hints.title: 3 · Review negative paths
hints.body: Exercise missing identity, foreign tickets, non-supervisors, repeated transitions, malformed reasons, and unexpected storage errors.

criteria.title: Identity and disclosure
criteria.target: Use strict gateway identity and organization-scoped lookup before role checks.
criteria.probe: Why should a foreign ticket return 404 for an ordinary agent?
criteria.practice: Write a role × tenant × ticket-state matrix.

criteria.title: State and audit integrity
criteria.target: Exactly one audit accompanies a successful state transition; storage failures roll back.
criteria.probe: What happens when audit persistence fails after the ticket changes?
criteria.practice: Inject a persistence failure and verify both records.

criteria.title: Compatibility and validation
criteria.target: Preserve exact response fields, trimmed reason limits, and error semantics.
criteria.probe: Which unknown attributes would become dangerous under mass assignment?
criteria.practice: Test malformed envelopes and Unicode boundaries.

criteria.title: Debugging discipline
criteria.target: Tie fixes to a reproduced failure and distinguish transaction guarantees from database locking.
criteria.probe: Would this SQLite test prove two PostgreSQL requests cannot race?
criteria.practice: Explain unique constraints, row locks and a real concurrency test.

follow_up: Allow a supervisor to reverse an escalation. Define the audit history, authorization and retry semantics before implementing it.
